reconcile.connective: Defenders read 2 Samuel 21:19 as a copyist's slip, restoring "brother of Goliath" from the parallel in 1 Chronicles 20:5 so David remains the giant's slayer.

discrepancy.connective: Baruch Halpern presses that the Masoretic text of 2 Samuel 21:19 plainly has Elhanan kill Goliath with no "brother" in it, so the Chronicler's added phrase is itself the harmonizing fix, not the original reading.

skeptic.name: Baruch Halpern
skeptic.work: David's Secret Demons: Messiah, Murderer, Traitor, King
skeptic.attribution: Baruch Halpern, David's Secret Demons: Messiah, Murderer, Traitor, King (2001)

excerpts.excerpt_text: the word "brother" is rightly supplied from Ch1 20:5; where his name is said to be Lahmi, for not Goliath himself was slain, though some so interpret it, and take Elhanan to be David; so Jarchi, and with which agrees the Targum; but he was slain not at Gob, but in the valley of Elah, nor had David any such name as Elhanan …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers 'Who killed Goliath?' by harmonizing 2 Sam 21:19 with 1 Sam 17 via the Chronicler's 'brother' (Lahmi), denying Elhanan=David and that Goliath himself was slain here. Strongest single reconcile; parity-capped to one on this discrepancy_first row.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on 2 Samuel 21:19
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this exact verse, calling it a transcriber's corruption and restoring the 1 Chronicles 20:5 reading (Lahmi, brother of Goliath) on the authority of Kennicott so that David, not Elhanan, slew Goliath.
